biography.plain_text: Iskandar Safa was a French-Lebanese businessman who built Privinvest with his brother Akram, creating an international group of naval shipyards. Trained in civil engineering at the American University of Beirut and business administration at INSEAD, he first made his fortune arranging international trade deals. His wider interests included property, hotels and media.

biography.html: Iskandar Safa was a French-Lebanese businessman who built Privinvest with his brother Akram, creating an international group of naval shipyards. Trained in civil engineering at the American University of Beirut and business administration at INSEAD, he first made his fortune arranging international trade deals. His wider interests included property, hotels and media.

long_biography.plain_text:
The acquisition of the struggling Cherbourg shipyard CMN gave Iskandar Safa a route from dealmaking into industrial ownership. He used his international business relationships to win naval contracts and rebuild activity at the yard. The business expanded into a group with shipbuilding operations in France and Germany, alongside engineering and support services.

His expansion into Mozambique brought a lasting legal controversy. After his death, a 2024 English civil judgment found that he and Privinvest had bribed the country's finance minister to secure state guarantees for maritime projects. The court reserved questions concerning his estate, distinguishing those proceedings from the findings against the companies.

confidence.reason: Acquisition and industrial expansion supported by institutional biography and contemporary reports. Court findings and express estate reservation stated narrowly; no criminal conviction claimed.
